brief:
Tonight is Push A — the same Push A your card has been holding since yesterday morning. You have not trained since Friday the 5th, so nothing new has been logged, and that is the single most important thing on this page: not one number below has moved. All three trainers re-read the same evidence they read yesterday and all three came back with the same calls, on purpose. This app has a rule that when no new session arrives, the numbers stand — re-deriving them every morning from the same log is how you end up with four different answers in four days.

So here is the card, unchanged. The opener is dumbbells, not the smith machine: 40 for eight to find the bench angle, then 45 for eight, twice. Three sets, not four. Forty-five is what you pressed for eight, three sets running, on 27 August, and it is what the overhead press honestly became on 2 September when you did it with dumbbells and 50 broke down to five reps. There is no smith machine in your new gym, so the 175 and 180 this app would print on its own belong to a building you left.

Chest press stays anchored to the only reading you have from the new machine: 127.5 and 142.5 for twelve, then 157.5 for ten. The top weight is exactly what you did on 2 September — nothing there goes up, only the reps come back into the range the program asks for. Rear delts stay at 100 for thirteen, 100 for twelve, then 90 for fourteen. Overhead triceps stays at 55 across all three sets; the job is finishing the third set, not adding weight. Rope pushdown stays at 45 for fifteen, twice. Crossovers, shoulder press and lateral raises each stay at the same weight with one more rep per set.

Five days off means you arrive fresh, which your recovery trainer said out loud makes tonight a better night to establish the new-gym baseline than to cut anything further. It did not change a single load because of the layoff, and neither did I.

Two things you should hear plainly. Your bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August, sixteen days ago, at 207. With the show on 1 March that is the one number nothing else in this app can give me. Step on the scale this week. And your Push A on 27 August ended part-way through the sixth lift, so the lateral raise and the rope pushdown got no sets at all — that is why your program trainer has put a card on your plan screen asking to drop the rope pushdown from Push A entirely, and another asking to move the lateral raise earlier in the night.

There are seven Yes/No cards waiting on your plan screen and none of them have been answered yet. Four are the same problem: four of your six sessions still open with a lift named for a smith machine you no longer have. The Push A one is tonight's and it is the awkward one — there is no incline press anywhere in your exercise list, so the only honest swap your program trainer can offer is assisted dips, and you skipped dips on 2 September, so that station may not exist there either. If it does not, answer No and say so, because the real fix is adding an incline press to the list and no trainer here can add one.

The seventh card is not a change at all — it is your program trainer answering the question you wrote on 17 August about corrective work. Its answer is that you have three corrective-role lifts (face pulls on both pull days, hip adductor and abductor on both leg days) but every one of them is either below the waist or in the rowing plane, and there is no shoulder-rotation or anti-rotation movement anywhere in the app's exercise list for it to put on a card.

Conditioning: easy cardio twice this week, twenty to thirty minutes.

flags.note: Nothing new has been logged since Friday 5 September, so tonight's card is yesterday's card unchanged — every trainer re-read the same evidence and made the same calls on purpose.
Your card would print 175 pounds on a smith incline press and 180 on the chest press if left alone — both old-gym numbers for machines you no longer use. Tonight's opener is dumbbells instead.
Bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August, sixteen days ago, at 207. With the show on 1 March this is the trend nothing else in the app can give me.
Your 27 August Push A ended part-way through the sixth lift, so the lateral raise and rope pushdown got no sets. Two cards on your plan screen address that.
Meso 2, week 3 of 4, a build block. All three trainers reported; five disagreements, all settled, and one fatigue objection upheld.
Seven Yes/No cards are waiting on your plan screen and none have been answered yet. Four of your six sessions still open with a smith-machine lift.

proposals.why: Your new gym has no smith machine and your exercise list has no incline press at all, so tonight's opener becomes assisted dips at 4 sets of 8 to 12 — the only chest compound left in the list that needs no smith machine and no new load history, since it is bodyweight; answer No if the new gym has no dip station either and I will find you something else.

On 2 September you pressed dumbbells at 45 and 50 into a slot still named for a smith machine the new gym does not have, so this renames it to the dumbbell shoulder press you are actually doing — 4 sets of 8 to 10 instead of the smith bar's 6 to 8.

Pull B still opens with a smith row the new gym does not have and your list has no barbell row to rename it to, so it becomes the wide seated cable row at 4 sets of 8 to 10 — heavier and lower-rep than the same row on Pull A.

You already ran this slot with a barbell on 5 September and wrote so on the card, but it is still named Smith RDL and your list has no RDL, so it becomes the deadlift at 4 sets of 8 to 10 — same four sets you did, lighter and higher-rep than your Pull A sets of 5 to 6.

Push A is eight lifts long and on 27 August it stopped part-way through the sixth, so the rope pushdown — your second triceps isolation of the night, sitting dead last behind three sets of overhead extensions — got none of its sets at all, and on 17 August, the one Push A you did finish, it went backwards inside the set: 52.5 for fifteen, then 47.5 for thirteen, then 47.5 for eleven.

Open question for you, not a change: you asked on 17 August why there are no corrective exercises in the program, and the accurate answer is that there are three — face pulls here on Pull A and again on Pull B, and the hip adductor and abductor on both leg days — but they are all either below the waist or a rowing-plane pull, and there is no shoulder-rotation or anti-rotation movement anywhere in the app's exercise list for me to put on a card, so this slot stays exactly as it is until that list itself is changed, which is a change to the app and needs your word rather than mine.

Carried forward unanswered for a second day: the cable lateral raise is your only side-delt work on Push A and it sits seventh of eight, so on 27 August the session ended before you reached it — this moves it to fifth, straight after the shoulder press.

overrides.reason: There is no smith machine at your new gym, so the 175 and 180 this card was about to print belong to a building you left. Do this on dumbbells: 40 for eight to find the bench angle, then 45 for eight twice. Forty-five is what you pressed for eight three sets running on 27 August, and incline is a stronger position than overhead, where 50 broke down to five reps on 2 September. Three sets, not four. Tonight is for writing down a real incline number, not defending an old one.

The 165, 172.5 and 180 this card wanted are the old gym's stack. Your only reading from this machine is 2 September — 97.5, 127.5 and 157.5 for eight each. The top weight here is unchanged from that night; the only thing asked is the ten to twelve reps your program has always asked for. If the numbers on the machine read differently, log what it says.

You paid for the jump to 17.5 on 27 August with reps — fifteen, fifteen, fifteen at the old weight became twelve, twelve, twelve at the new one. So the weight stays and the reps come back: one more per set before anything moves again.

A 45-pound dumbbell weighs 45 pounds in any building, so this is the one lift tonight the gym change cannot touch. You did eight, eight and eight on 27 August, which is the bottom of the range. Nine each before the weight moves.

You earned this one outright: fifteen, fifteen and fifteen at 90 on 27 August. You took the step on 2 September and got 100 for thirteen, then had to drop to 90 for fourteen and stopped at two sets. Tonight asks for the same two sets plus the third one you did not reach.

The card wanted 57.5 for three sets off a single set on 27 August. On 2 September you got 55 for eleven, then ten, then dropped to 50. This is 55 across all three, which is exactly what you did on 3 August. The job is the third set, not the weight.

Not logged since 17 August, and it faded inside that session — thirteen, twelve, then eleven. Same 10, one more rep on each set. It is the only side-delt work on this day, which is why there is a card on your plan screen asking to move it earlier.

This has been sliding for a month: 60 in July, 52.5 then a collapse to 47.5 for thirteen and eleven on 17 August. So it resets one notch below the weight that actually broke, over the two sets this slot now carries instead of three. Your recovery trainer wanted 27.5 on the theory the new stack reads lower; I checked and it does not — your reverse-grip pushdown read 25 here and 27.5 there, and your overhead triceps reads 55 in both.

dissent.progression: Hold the old figures — 175 for seven three times and 180 for eight — because reps went backwards at 175 on 27 August so nothing was earned, and the new gym's incline station has never been read.
dissent.recovery: Refuse the smith number entirely and establish a dumbbell baseline: 40 for eight, then 45 for eight twice, three sets.
dissent.why: Unchanged from yesterday's ruling, and I re-checked it rather than copying it. Progression's own reasoning still defeats it: it wrote that the new station has never been read, then prescribed a load measured on a machine that does not exist in the building. He has had no smith machine since 2 September, by his own note. The one comparable transfer we have watched — smith overhead press at 105 to 135 on the bar becoming 45 on dumbbells and missing at 50 — says the carried figure would have been roughly four times the honest one. Recovery filed this as a fatigue objection, which is the truthful label and one I am allowed to overrule. I chose not to.

dissent.progression: Re-anchor to the new machine's only reading and earn the prescribed rep range at an unchanged top pin: 127.5 and 142.5 for twelve, 157.5 for ten.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 2 September verbatim — 97.5, 127.5 and 157.5 for eight each — because the number is measuring the machine and not the man.
dissent.why: Both seats agree the old 165 to 180 is dead, so the disagreement is only about what to ask of the new reading. Recovery's fear is that a raise here is a guess, but progression does not raise the top weight at all — 157.5 stays exactly where he left it. What it asks for is ten to twelve reps, which is what this slot has prescribed all along and which he has not yet met on this machine. A second night at eight earns nothing in week three of a build block, and 97.5 and 127.5 were plainly the ramp up to the top set, not working weights.

dissent.progression: Take the step he earned: 100 for thirteen, 100 for twelve, then 90 for fourteen.
dissent.recovery: Roll back to 90 for fifteen three times, because three sets at 100 has never happened anywhere.
dissent.why: Recovery is describing an ask nobody made. Progression does not want three sets at 100; it wants the two he already produced plus the third set he skipped, at the 90 he dropped to himself. The raise was earned cleanly — fifteen, fifteen and fifteen at 90 on 27 August — and taken successfully on 2 September at the new gym, so this is not a cross-building guess. Undoing a raise a week after he earned it is the more expensive mistake here.

dissent.progression: 55 for eleven, eleven and ten — finish the third set at the weight, do not chase 57.5.
dissent.recovery: Drop to 50 for twelve across three sets.
dissent.why: Progression's prescription is not a raise. He produced 55 for eleven and 55 for ten on 2 September before dropping to 50, and 57.5 for twelve on 27 August. Recovery's 50 is below work he has repeatedly completed, and its worry about the new gym's stack does not survive the log: this lift read 55 at the old gym and 55 again at the new one on 2 September. Same scale, proven weight, one unfinished set to close.

dissent.progression: Cut to 45 for fifteen, twice — one notch below the 47.5 that collapsed, over the slot's current two sets.
dissent.recovery: Cut much harder, to 27.5, because the new gym's pushdown station read 27.5 on 2 September.
dissent.why: I checked recovery's premise again today and it is still wrong. 27.5 is his reverse-grip pushdown weight, not a scale artifact: that lift read 25 at the old gym on 23 August and 27.5 at the new one on 2 September, which is a rep-earned step up, not a stack change. His overhead cable extension reads 55 in both buildings. The cable stack has not changed scale, so cutting a rope pushdown to a reverse-grip weight would ask about a third of the right load. Both seats agree the lift needs cutting after 17 August; progression's is the cut the evidence supports.
